Fibonacci Numbers in an Equilateral Triangle

SequencesAreaAlgebra
Game: A big triangle made of tiny triangles is coloured in a pattern of flat-topped shapes; there is nothing to win or lose.
How to play: Change the size N with the box or the up and down arrow keys, and read the list of shapes under the picture.
    Look for the math

    Colour the top triangle of a triangular lattice, then the next one down on the right, then trapezoids hanging alternately from the left and right edges. The sizes of the rows they end on, and the sides of every trapezoid, are Fibonacci numbers.

    A trapezoid with 60 degree angles

    Cut a trapezoid with 60° base angles. Each slanted side leans out by half its length at each end, so base = top + leg. That is the Fibonacci rule Fk+2 = Fk + Fk+1 in disguise. The logic test measured every shape from its corners for every N the applet offers (5 to 145) and found top, leg and base to be three consecutive Fibonacci numbers: (1,1,2), (1,2,3), (2,3,5), (3,5,8), ….

    Why the next one fits

    Each trapezoid ends on a row whose number is the next Fibonacci number, and the next one starts on that row: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, … The next top is the leg that went before, so the shapes stack with no gaps, and the test checked that every shape starts on the row where the one above ended. The applet stops when the next row would be past N.

    Counting unit triangles

    A trapezoid is a big triangle of side base with a small one of side top cut off, so it holds base² − top² = leg × (base + top) unit triangles: the trapezoid with top 21, sides 34 and base 55 has 55² − 21² = 2584.

    The applet's two shapes at the very top (a unit triangle on each edge) are the degenerate trapezoids with top 0; the numbering of the page's rhombi (sides 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, …) is not drawn by the applet and is not shown here.

    Set N to 145 and read the list from the top. What is the next trapezoid after top 34, sides 55, base 89?

    Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
